542ce04b-10de-4062-8f5a-ee8888ab05ad: Batch Gradient Descent - Weight updation: After all the records (rows) i.e, at the end of every epoch
Stochastic Gradient Descent - Weight Updation: After each and every record (row) in an epoch.
Mini-Batch Gradient Descent - Weight Updation: After batch-size number of record(s) (row(s)) in an epoch.

Stochastic Gradient Descent with Momentum - Weight Updation: After each and every record (row) in an epoch, but indirectly, i.e considering updation caused by past records as well (I am carrying it out similar to SGD)

Nesterov Accelerated Gradient Descent - Weight Updation: After each and every record (row) in an epoch, but indirectly in two steps, first by only the history then by the current derivative of the loss function w.r.t weight(s).
Adagrad - Weight Updation: After each and every record (row) in an epoch, but learning rate changes over time
AdaDelta-RMSprop - Weight Updation: After each and every record (row) in an epoch, but learning rate changes over time gradually
Adam - Weight Updation: After each and every record (row) in an epoch, but learning rate changes over time gradually and so does the weights
Collective Comparisons are done using: i) Weights v/s Epochs ii) Bias v/s Epochs iii) Mean Squared Error v/s Epochs
Conclusion: Hence it can be seen that the Adam optimization technique is the best performing optimization.

8a91a91c-c5b0-446a-af9e-eab841c6116d:
Parameters
N: Number of nodes in the graph
p: Probability of edge formation between nodes

When changing (increasing) the number of nodes in a network, while not changing the probability of edges forming between any, we see that the Diameter and the Average Clustering Coefficient (ACC) do not change significantly.
Diameter does seems to slowly decrease, could be interpreted as new nodes providing shorter direct paths than the previous shorter paths.
While, if we change the probability for a constant number of nodes, Diameter of the network decreases and the ACC increases.
